triples.subject: Father Zossima
triples.quote: Alyosha lived in the cell of the elder, who was very fond of him and let him wait upon him.

triples.subject: Father Zossima
triples.quote: The elder Zossima was sixty-five. He came of a family of landowners, had been in the army in early youth, and served in the Caucasus as an officer.

triples.subject: Father Zossima
triples.quote: for he fully believed in the spiritual power of his teacher and rejoiced in his fame, in his glory, as though it were his own triumph.

triples.subject: Alyosha
triples.quote: He more quickly made friends with his half-brother Dmitri (though he arrived later) than with his own brother Ivan.

triples.subject: Alyosha
triples.quote: He more quickly made friends with his half-brother Dmitri (though he arrived later) than with his own brother Ivan.

triples.subject: Dmitri
triples.quote: From him Alyosha learnt all the details of the important affair which had of late formed such a close and remarkable bond between the two elder brothers.

triples.subject: Fyodor Pavlovitch
triples.quote: It was at this time that the discord between Dmitri and his father seemed at its acutest stage and their relations had become insufferably strained.

triples.subject: Fyodor Pavlovitch
triples.quote: It must be noted that he was not, like Ivan, staying with his father, but living apart at the other end of the town.

triples.subject: Fyodor Pavlovitch
triples.quote: while his father might be contemplating some piece of buffoonery. Though he said nothing, Alyosha thoroughly understood his father.

triples.subject: Dmitri
triples.quote: It was at this time that the discord between Dmitri and his father seemed at its acutest stage and their relations had become insufferably strained.

triples.subject: Alyosha
triples.quote: He only sent word the day before, through a friend, to his brother Dmitri, that he loved him and expected him to keep his promise.
